item.text:
**8B.1 Research Note**
Bottom line: Kishida’s 2024 public record shows a fairly clear governing program, not a vacuum. The center of gravity is a technocratic, pro-growth, pro-child-support, pro-disaster-recovery, and hard-security agenda wrapped in “New Form of Capitalism” rhetoric. The main negative evidence is not an alternative ideology, but survival politics: scandal management, compromise with conservative blocs, and repeated emphasis on restoring trust.

**Positive**
- [New Year’s Reflection by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/01nentou.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-01 | Kishida set out a broad 2024 direction: break from deflation, defend people’s daily lives against price rises, pursue active summit diplomacy, strengthen security, and restore public trust so policies can be carried out. This is direct evidence of an articulated governing strategy, not just reactive administration. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | The speech lays out a coherent program: disaster response, wage growth, New Form of Capitalism, child support, fiscal reform, digital administration, and defense/security buildup. It is the clearest 2024 statement of a governing agenda that can be checked against later action. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [A New Form of Capitalism](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/newcapitalism.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 | Kishida’s official policy page defines his program as building an economy and society suited to a new era, with structural wage growth, human-capital investment, labor-market reform, and broader middle-class expansion. This is the strongest programmatic evidence for a durable governing ideology. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [Outgoing Japanese leader urges ruling party to embrace change](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/outgoing-japanese-leader-urges-ruling-party-to-embrace-change-3571057) | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | Kishida framed his exit as part of showing the LDP had changed and urged the party to choose a transformative successor. That reveals a political strategy centered on trust restoration and controlled transition, which still reflects an intentional governing logic. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [Statement by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio upon the General Resignation of the Kishida Cabinet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202410/1001danwa.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-10-01 | Kishida summarized his term as economic revival, defense strengthening, and political reform, then emphasized accountability after the fundraising scandal. This is retrospective evidence that he understood his cabinet as pursuing a defined agenda with identifiable pillars. | QIDs: 8B.1

**Negative / Mixed**
- [Japan's Prime Minister Kishida to resign, paving way for new leader](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455) | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | Reuters reported that Kishida stepped down because of public disaffection over scandals and rising living costs. That weakens any claim that his program was dominant or consistently persuasive, and suggests political survival pressures were shaping his agenda. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [Kishida’s legacy: Scandals and compromise at home, global respect for security and diplomacy](https://kyma.com/news/2024/09/30/kishidas-legacy-scandals-and-compromise-at-home-global-respect-for-security-and-diplomacy/) | Associated Press | 2024-09-30 | AP described Kishida at home as “a leader without a vision” who compromised with powerful conservative nationalists to stay in power. That is strong mixed evidence: it points to coalition maintenance and power management more than a clear, self-contained ideology. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [Japan's Prime Minister Kishida to resign, paving way for new leader](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-3570455) | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | Reuters said Kishida’s term was marred by political scandals and that his support eroded as disclosures around faction finances and the Unification Church mounted. This does not refute a program, but it shows the program operated under severe legitimacy strain and was partly subordinated to damage control. | QIDs: 8B.1
- [What to know about the party vote that will determine Japan’s next leader](https://halifax.citynews.ca/2024/09/26/what-to-know-about-the-party-vote-that-will-determine-japans-next-leader/) | Associated Press | 2024-09-26 | AP’s framing of the LDP as faction-driven, with kingmakers shaping outcomes, is structural evidence that Kishida governed inside a power network rather than a cleanly ideological movement. That limits how far one can read his program as a coherent doctrine instead of elite bargaining. | QIDs: 8B.1

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence that Kishida articulated a recognizable governing program in 2024, especially around “New Form of Capitalism,” wage growth, child support, fiscal reform, disaster recovery, and defense/security.
- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence of an explicit regime-control ideology or a formal doctrine centered on power for its own sake.
- The negative evidence is mostly indirect: coalition compromise, factional politics, scandal pressure, and trust erosion. That means the record is better described as programmatic but politically constrained, not ideologically hollow and not overtly regime-control oriented.
